candidates.attacker_control: Any authenticated user can fully control the multipart form fields resumableFilename, resumableIdentifier, resumableChunkNumber, resumableTotalChunks and resumableTotalSize, plus the uploaded chunk bytes, on multipart POSTs to /submit; resumableFilename/resumableIdentifier/resumableChunkNumber are also accepted as query parameters on GET. Values are used verbatim in File path construction (path separators and ".." are not filtered; no canonical-path/startsWith check exists).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched all occurrences of resumableFilename/resumableIdentifier/resumableChunkNumber: no sanitization, whitelisting, normalization or containment check exists anywhere in the snapshot. The FileUploadRequest.getFilename helper strips only text up to the last OS separator and is applied only to the simple-upload branch, not to makeFileFromChunks (which uses the raw parameter). The tempDir prefix prevents absolute paths from being honored, but relative "../" traversal is not prevented, and createNewFile() returning false does not stop FileOutputStream from truncating an existing target. /submit is behind the registered-only filter (web.xml lines 104-107 and RegisteredOnlyFilter), so this is not anonymous, which lowers severity but still crosses a privilege boundary. The chunk-write branch requires the target directory to pre-exist and the assembly branch requires all chunks plus a size check, which are real but attacker-satisfiable constraints.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file create/overwrite with attacker-controlled content as the web application OS user. Depending on which directories are writable this can overwrite served resources or configuration/state, destroy or corrupt data, or place executable content in a directory the container serves/executes (the repository's own Dockerfile runs Tomcat with the deployed webapps under /dspace, so a write into a deployed web application can lead to remote code execution). At minimum it is a high-integrity/availability compromise from a low-privileged (registered user) starting point.
candidates.prerequisites: An account on the JSPUI (the /submit mapping is protected only by the registered-only filter, and self-registration is a normal configuration) and a network-reachable JSPUI. Exploitation additionally requires the servlet-container OS user to have write permission to the chosen target path; for the FileUploadRequest chunk-write variant the target directory must already exist (or be creatable by the single-level mkdir in DoGetResumable), and for makeFileFromChunks the chunk directory and all part files must exist and their total size must be >= resumableTotalSize.
candidates.root_cause: The resumable-upload flow uses request-controlled strings as filesystem path components without sanitization or containment checks. SubmissionController.makeFileFromChunks builds the destination path as tmpDir + File.separator + request.getParameter("resumableFilename") and writes attacker-supplied chunk bytes with new FileOutputStream(destFile) (the createNewFile() result is ignored, so existing files are also overwritten). SubmissionController.doPostResumable/DoGetResumable similarly build directory and chunk paths from raw resumableIdentifier and resumableChunkNumber, and FileUploadRequest writes each uploaded chunk to tempDir + File.separator + resumableIdentifier + File.separator + "part" + resumableChunkNumber when that directory exists. A value containing "../" escapes the configured temp directory.
candidates.title: Authenticated path traversal / arbitrary file write via unsanitized resumable-upload parameters in JSPUI SubmissionController and FileUploadRequest
candidates.trace: Request to /submit (GET or POST) -> SubmissionController.doDSGet/doDSPost (dispatch at lines 216-222 and 250-260 when resumableFilename is non-empty) -> doPostResumable lines 1650-1655 computes chunkDirPath = tempDir + separator + resumableIdentifier -> makeFileFromChunks lines 1700-1712 computes destFilePath = tmpDir + separator + resumableFilename, then createNewFile()/new FileOutputStream(destFile) writes the concatenated attacker chunk bytes to that path. In parallel, FileUploadRequest lines 98-111 writes each uploaded part to tempDir + separator + resumableIdentifier + separator + "part" + resumableChunkNumber whenever the containing directory exists, again using the raw parameter values. Because the values may contain "../", the write leaves the upload temp directory and lands in any directory writable by the application user.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-tested (no build/execution permitted). RCE-level impact depends on the deployment's filesystem permissions and on whether a writable directory is served/executed by the container; a shared temp directory can also introduce cross-user interference. I could not determine which specific upstream fix/CVE this snapshot predates, so the exact expected annotation is uncertain.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal) leading to arbitrary file write; potential remote code execution (CWE-434/CWE-94 depending on deployment layout)

coverage_summary: Read get_source_scope (2286 model-visible files; binary files skipped; parity with P1). Mapped JSPUI entry points and filters from web.xml, then read ~20 servlets (SubmissionController, FileUploadRequest, BitstreamServlet, RetrieveServlet, HTMLServlet, HandleServlet, SitemapServlet, StatisticsServlet, DisplayStatisticsServlet, OpenSearch/Discovery, ItemExportArchiveServlet, BatchImportServlet, JSONServlet, FeedbackServlet, AuthorityChooseServlet, ControlledVocabularySearchServlet, DSpaceServlet, RegisteredOnlyFilter, Authenticate, JSPManager, invalid-id.jsp, internal.jsp) plus web.xml mappings. Traced dspace-api sinks for the submission/upload path (UploadStep, ItemImport unzip/processUIImport/loadXML, packager/METS ingesters, OpenSearch output), batch import, sitemap/statistics/export, and used search_code across all modules for SQL statement concatenation, Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder, ObjectInputStream, File/FileInputStream/FileOutputStream, URL.openConnection/openStream, sendRedirect, XML parser construction, ZipEntry usage and getParameter sinks. dspace-rest and dspace-xmlui were sampled via targeted searches rather than fully read. File-level coverage is therefore broad but not exhaustive.
limitations: No build, static-analysis tooling, or runtime testing was performed; all conclusions are source-level only and none is runtime-confirmed.

The snapshot's version is inferred from pom.xml/build.properties (DSpace 5.10); no git metadata is present to identify the exact commit or which later security fix it precedes, so the intended ground-truth issue for this case is uncertain.

Exploitability of the file-write candidate depends on deployment-specific write permissions of the servlet-container user and on which directories are served or executed; this cannot be determined from source alone.

Coverage was search-driven for large modules (dspace-xmlui Cocoon internals, dspace-oai, sword/swordv2, dspace-lni, dspace-solr configuration, JSP views) and may have missed issues in files not reached by the patterns above.
No dependency/SBOM (CVE) analysis was performed; third-party library vulnerabilities are out of scope for this source review.
Per the one-candidate limit, other plausible-but-weaker issues are recorded only as rejected leads, not as additional candidates.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip Slip in ItemImport.unzip (dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/app/itemimport/ItemImport.java lines 2025-2085): zip entry names are appended to zipDir and written with FileOutputStream with no ".." validation, and inputType=saf additionally downloads an admin-supplied URL (line 2218) before unzipping.
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine arbitrary-file-write/SSRF pattern, but reachable only from the admin-only /dspace-admin/batchimport servlet (AdminOnlyFilter), the XMLUI administrative batch import flow, or the CLI; it does not cross the same low-privilege boundary as the selected candidate, and the batch import runs privileged regardless.

rejected_leads.lead: Unhardened XML parsing / XXE in package import and related parsers (e.g., ItemImport.loadXML near line 1951, METSManifest.create line 254, AbstractMETSIngester/METS ingestion, authority XMLUtils), which use DocumentBuilderFactory/SAXBuilder without external-entity hardening while processing uploaded packages.
rejected_leads.reason: Real hardening weaknesses, but the attacker must be able to supply an ingested package (admin batch import, CLI packager, or authenticated SWORD deposit); no evidence in this snapshot of an unauthenticated or ordinary-user path, so impact/likelihood is weaker than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: SitemapServlet 'map' parameter used in a filesystem path (dspace-jspui/.../SitemapServlet.java lines 69-82) on the unauthenticated /sitemap and /htmlmap endpoints.
rejected_leads.reason: User-controlled value is concatenated without validation, but a fixed .html or .xml.gz suffix is appended and a 'sitemap' prefix is added, so only files matching those names/extensions under the sitemap directory (and reachable via traversal) can be read; I could not demonstrate a meaningful disclosure target.

rejected_leads.lead: OpenURLServlet concatenates user parameters into a redirect Location without URL-encoding (dspace-jspui/.../OpenURLServlet.java lines 38-70).
rejected_leads.reason: The redirect target is context-relative (no open redirect), and the reflected query is HTML-escaped where it is rendered in the search JSPs; header-splitting is also blocked by modern containers. No clear exploitable impact found.

rejected_leads.lead: Item export download filename parsing (ItemExport.canDownload lines 1218-1239; getExportDownloadInputStream lines 1148-1161; ItemExportArchiveServlet and XMLUI ItemExportDownloadReader).
rejected_leads.reason: The authorization check parses the eperson ID out of the filename between the last '_' and last '.' and then concatenates the filename into a download path, which looks traversal-prone, but the target file must already exist and its name must match the user's ID pattern; no reliable arbitrary-file-read path was established.

rejected_leads.lead: JSP views reflecting request parameters (e.g., eperson-browse.jsp 'sortby' hidden field, controlledvocabulary pages, feedback/suggest pages).
rejected_leads.reason: Several unescaped echoes exist but the clearest one is on an admin page and/or requires a crafted link be followed by the victim; not enough evidence to prefer over the selected filesystem-write issue.

summary: Defensive review of the DSpace 5.10 source snapshot (2286 files; dspace-api, dspace-jspui, dspace-xmlui, dspace-rest, dspace-oai, sword/swordv2, lni, solr, modules). I mapped the JSPUI web.xml entry points and filters, then traced request parameters into filesystem, SQL, XML and network sinks. The single strongest candidate is the resumable-upload handling in the JSPUI: attacker-supplied resumableFilename/resumableIdentifier/resumableChunkNumber values are concatenated directly into filesystem paths and written with FileOutputStream, giving any registered user arbitrary file write path traversal (potential RCE depending on write permissions). Other genuine-looking issues (Zip Slip in ItemImport.unzip, unhardened XML parsing in package import, limited SitemapServlet traversal) were considered and are listed as rejected leads because they require admin/CLI access or are constrained. No SQL injection, command injection, or deserialization issue of comparable strength was found. Findings are source-evidence based only; nothing was executed or runtime-confirmed.
